candidates: In Storybook's multi-pass preset pipeline, a config value read from an early `presets.apply('core', {})` call can differ from the value used by runtime enforcement if a later preset pass overrides it. When emitting `logger.warn` messages or populating startup-output data that reflects an enforced config value, re-read that value from the same (final) preset pass used for enforcement rather than reusing a value captured in an earlier pass.

Keep JSDoc comments on exported config interfaces (e.g., `CoreConfig` in `code/core/src/types/modules/core-common.ts`) accurate whenever the scope of a feature expands. If a field's behavior changes — for example, validation that previously applied only to one transport now applies to multiple — update the comment to reflect the full, current behavior before merging.
Proofread prose in Markdown documentation files (e.g., files under `.github/workflows/`) for typos before merging.

CHANGELOG entries for security or behavioral changes must be specific: name every affected component or mechanism (e.g., both HTTP and WebSocket if both are affected), avoid vague labels like 'Add request validation', and include a link to the PR (e.g., `[#12345](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/12345)`).
